primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: MCAD deficiency impairs mitochondrial beta-oxidation of medium-chain fatty acids, causing fasting intolerance, hypoketotic hypoglycemia, and dicarboxylic acid accumulation.
vignette: An 18-month-old child becomes lethargic after a viral illness with poor intake. Blood glucose is 38 mg/dL and serum ketones are unexpectedly low.
correct: Mitochondrial beta-oxidation of medium-chain fatty acids
distractor_notes: Glycolysis remains functional; the problem emerges during fasting when fatty acid oxidation is needed.
Urea-cycle defects cause hyperammonemia.
Glycogen synthesis defects do not specifically cause hypoketotic hypoglycemia.
The pentose phosphate pathway generates NADPH and is unrelated to MCAD deficiency.
key_expl: MCAD deficiency prevents efficient medium-chain fatty acid oxidation during fasting, limiting ketone production and glucose preservation.
objective: Recognize hypoketotic fasting hypoglycemia as a fatty acid oxidation defect.

sources.title: Medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes impaired medium-chain fatty acid oxidation causing hypoketotic hypoglycemia.

sources.title: ACADM gene
sources.support: ACADM encodes the enzyme initiating beta-oxidation of medium-chain fatty acids.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency blocks the final step of glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, causing severe fasting hypoglycemia, lactic acidosis, hyperuricemia, and hepatomegaly.
vignette: A 6-month-old infant has fasting hypoglycemia, hepatomegaly, lactic acidosis, hyperuricemia, and hypertriglyceridemia.
distractor_notes: Muscle glycogen phosphorylase deficiency causes McArdle disease.
Hexokinase/glucokinase catalyzes glucose phosphorylation and is not the defect in type I glycogen storage disease.
Pyruvate dehydrogenase defects cause lactic acidosis but not this glycogen-storage pattern.
Lactate conversion is not the primary defect.
key_expl: Glucose-6-phosphatase releases free glucose from glucose-6-phosphate in liver and kidney; deficiency traps substrate and causes fasting hypoglycemia.
objective: Identify the blocked reaction in von Gierke disease.
clues: hepatomegaly with lactic acidosis and hyperuricemia

sources.title: Glycogen storage disease type I
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes glucose-6-phosphatase system defects causing GSD I.

sources.title: G6PC1 gene
sources.support: G6PC1 encodes glucose-6-phosphatase, which produces free glucose from glucose-6-phosphate.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: HGPRT deficiency blocks salvage of hypoxanthine and guanine, increasing de novo purine synthesis and uric acid production while causing severe neurologic and behavioral abnormalities.
vignette: A 4-year-old boy has dystonia, developmental delay, self-biting behavior, and orange urate crystals in his diaper.
distractor_notes: Pyrimidine degradation defects do not cause hyperuricemia and self-injury.
Heme synthesis defects cause porphyrias or sideroblastic anemia.
Branched-chain oxidation defects cause MSUD.
Fatty acid oxidation defects cause fasting metabolic crises.
key_expl: HGPRT is a purine salvage enzyme; its deficiency causes Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.
objective: Connect self-injury and hyperuricemia to defective purine salvage.

sources.title: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes HPRT1 deficiency and impaired purine recycling.

sources.title: HPRT1 gene
sources.support: HPRT1 encodes HGPRT, a key purine salvage enzyme.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency impairs conversion of homocysteine to cystathionine, causing homocysteine accumulation, thrombosis, osteoporosis, and ectopia lentis.
vignette: A 12-year-old boy has developmental delay, severe myopia from downward lens displacement, osteoporosis, and a prior deep venous thrombosis.
distractor_notes: Phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency causes PKU.
Homocysteine is produced from methionine metabolism; the block is downstream at cystathionine formation.
Homogentisate metabolism is abnormal in alkaptonuria.
Branched-chain amino acid metabolism is abnormal in MSUD.
key_expl: CBS catalyzes homocysteine condensation with serine to form cystathionine.
objective: Identify the blocked transsulfuration reaction in homocystinuria.

sources.title: Homocystinuria
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes CBS deficiency and homocysteine accumulation.

sources.title: CBS gene
sources.support: CBS encodes cystathionine beta-synthase, which converts homocysteine toward cystathionine.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Homogentisate 1,2-dioxygenase deficiency causes homogentisic acid accumulation, darkening urine and depositing ochronotic pigment in cartilage.
vignette: A 45-year-old man has dark pigmentation of ear cartilage, chronic back stiffness, and urine that turns black after standing.
distractor_notes: Phenylalanine accumulates in PKU.
Methylmalonic acid rises in vitamin B12 deficiency and methylmalonic acidemia.
Galactose-1-phosphate accumulates in classic galactosemia.
Uric acid rises in purine overproduction disorders.
key_expl: Alkaptonuria results from homogentisate dioxygenase deficiency and homogentisic acid accumulation.
objective: Identify the stored metabolite in alkaptonuria.

sources.title: Alkaptonuria
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes homogentisic acid accumulation in alkaptonuria.

sources.title: HGD gene
sources.support: HGD encodes homogentisate 1,2-dioxygenase.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Biotinidase deficiency prevents efficient recycling of biotin, reducing activity of multiple biotin-dependent carboxylases and causing neurologic and cutaneous disease.
vignette: A 5-month-old infant has seizures, hypotonia, alopecia, and a scaly rash. Biotinidase activity is very low.
lead: Biotin normally functions primarily as a cofactor for which enzyme class?
distractor_notes: Biotin is not a general kinase cofactor.
Proteases use diverse catalytic mechanisms and do not rely on biotin as a class.
Phosphatases do not require biotin as their defining cofactor.
Biotin specifically carries activated carbon dioxide in carboxylation reactions.
key_expl: Biotin is a covalently bound cofactor for several carboxylase enzymes.
objective: Connect biotinidase deficiency with impaired carboxylase function.

sources.title: Biotinidase deficiency
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes impaired biotin recycling and reduced activity of biotin-dependent enzymes.

sources.title: BTD gene
sources.support: BTD encodes biotinidase, which recycles biotin for carboxylase enzymes.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: PEX gene defects impair peroxisome biogenesis, disrupting very-long-chain fatty acid oxidation and plasmalogen synthesis across multiple tissues.
vignette: A newborn has severe hypotonia, seizures, craniofacial abnormalities, hepatomegaly, and elevated very-long-chain fatty acids. Testing shows a PEX1 pathogenic variant.
distractor_notes: Lysosomal defects cause storage diseases such as Gaucher and Tay-Sachs.
Golgi defects do not explain the characteristic VLCFA accumulation.
Mitochondrial disorders can be multisystem but PEX1 specifically affects peroxisome assembly.
ER dysfunction is not the primary PEX1 lesion.
key_expl: PEX proteins are required for peroxisome biogenesis; loss produces Zellweger spectrum disease.
objective: Identify peroxisomal biogenesis failure in Zellweger syndrome.

sources.title: Zellweger spectrum disorder
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes PEX gene defects that impair peroxisome function.

sources.title: PEX1 gene
sources.support: PEX1 is required for normal peroxisome assembly and protein import.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Alpha-L-iduronidase deficiency causes lysosomal accumulation of dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate, producing coarse features, organomegaly, skeletal disease, and developmental decline.
vignette: A 2-year-old child has coarse facial features, hepatosplenomegaly, corneal clouding, developmental delay, and skeletal deformities.
lead: Which enzyme is most likely deficient?
distractor_notes: Iduronate sulfatase deficiency causes Hunter syndrome, which typically lacks corneal clouding.
Hexosaminidase A deficiency causes Tay-Sachs disease.
Glucocerebrosidase deficiency causes Gaucher disease.
Sphingomyelinase deficiency causes Niemann-Pick types A/B.
key_expl: Hurler syndrome is caused by IDUA deficiency and glycosaminoglycan accumulation.
objective: Differentiate Hurler from Hunter syndrome using enzyme defect and corneal clouding.

sources.title: Mucopolysaccharidosis type I
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes alpha-L-iduronidase deficiency causing MPS I.

sources.title: IDUA gene
sources.support: IDUA encodes alpha-L-iduronidase for lysosomal glycosaminoglycan degradation.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: NPC1 or NPC2 defects impair intracellular cholesterol and lipid trafficking from lysosomes, causing progressive neurodegeneration and visceral lipid accumulation.
vignette: A 10-year-old child has vertical gaze palsy, ataxia, cognitive decline, and hepatosplenomegaly. Genetic testing shows biallelic NPC1 variants.
correct: Intracellular trafficking of cholesterol from lysosomes
distractors: Degradation of GM2 ganglioside by hexosaminidase A
distractor_notes: GM2 degradation is defective in Tay-Sachs disease.
Glucocerebroside degradation is defective in Gaucher disease.
Peroxisomal VLCFA import is impaired in X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy.
MCAD deficiency impairs mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation.
key_expl: NPC1/NPC2 proteins mediate intracellular lipid trafficking; deficiency traps cholesterol and other lipids in lysosomal compartments.
objective: Identify defective lysosomal cholesterol trafficking in Niemann-Pick type C.

sources.title: Niemann-Pick disease type C
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes NPC1/2 defects impairing cellular cholesterol and lipid movement.

sources.title: NPC1 gene
sources.support: NPC1 is involved in movement of cholesterol and other lipids within cells.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: MEFV pathogenic variants dysregulate pyrin inflammasome activity and interleukin-1-mediated innate inflammation, causing recurrent self-limited fever and serositis.
vignette: A 16-year-old boy of Mediterranean ancestry has recurrent 1- to 3-day attacks of fever with severe abdominal and pleuritic chest pain, with complete recovery between attacks.
lead: Which immune mechanism is most directly implicated?
distractors: T-cell destruction of pancreatic beta cells
distractor_notes: IgE-mediated reactions cause allergy and anaphylaxis, not periodic serositis.
Antinuclear autoantibodies characterize systemic autoimmune disease, whereas FMF is autoinflammatory.
Terminal complement deficiency predisposes to Neisseria infection.
Beta-cell autoimmunity causes type 1 diabetes.
key_expl: FMF is an autoinflammatory disorder of pyrin/inflammasome regulation and IL-1 signaling.
objective: Distinguish autoinflammatory FMF from adaptive autoimmune disorders.

sources.title: Familial Mediterranean fever
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes MEFV-related recurrent autoinflammatory fever and serositis.

sources.title: MEFV gene
sources.support: MEFV encodes pyrin, a regulator of inflammatory signaling.
